taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Full occurrence-led review against VIGIL Failure Taxonomy 0.6.6 retains the occurrence as unclassified. VIGIL-FC-000032 Access-State Differentiation was tested because some Claude surfaces failed while others remained available, but the reporting explicitly distinguished the affected Claude website and Claude Code from the operational API and Cowork components. That representation preserves rather than collapses the material scope distinction, and no misleading recovery state is evidenced. VIGIL-FC-000031 Authentication-State Continuity is not established because login errors are reported without an expiry, revocation, refresh, recovery or credential-replacement transition failing to propagate coherently. VIGIL-FC-000048 Verification-Dependency Access Continuity is not established because no qualifying verifier or otherwise-valid entitlement blocked without fallback is evidenced. Generic bounded service unavailability does not fit another selectable class.

classification_review_provenance.authority_boundary: Taxonomy version reviewed: 0.6.6. Candidate classes tested: VIGIL-FC-000032, VIGIL-FC-000031 and VIGIL-FC-000048. Accepted mappings: none. FC-000032 is rejected because affected and operational components remained distinctly represented; FC-000031 is rejected because no authentication-state transition propagation defect is established; FC-000048 is rejected because no dependent verifier and no-fallback mechanism is established. No technical root cause is inferred from generic login, voice or chat errors.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Business Insider and TechRadar report that Anthropic declared a major outage on 7 April 2026 affecting Claude.ai and Claude Code. TechRadar preserved provider statements identifying login, voice and chat errors on desktop and mobile. Business Insider reported that Claude API and Cowork remained operational and that Anthropic applied a fix and restored normal success rates roughly 90 minutes after the disruption began; TechRadar's timestamped updates place the identified-to-fix window at about 56 minutes.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The occurrence demonstrates successful scope separation under degraded conditions: the provider status distinguished unavailable user and coding surfaces from operational API and Cowork components. That distinction supports targeted recovery and avoids falsely converting partial service degradation into a single undifferentiated access state. The unresolved governance issue is ordinary service resilience, for which the current selectable taxonomy does not supply a mechanism class on this evidence.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: This incident is a useful negative control for access-state classification. A multi-component outage can be operationally significant without being Access-State Differentiation when the provider keeps affected and unaffected surfaces legible. CAM should preserve component-level status, recovery timing and dependency boundaries while avoiding taxonomy inflation from outage severity alone.
